name: CY62128EV30LL-45SXIT
title: 1 Mbit (128K × 8) low-power asynchronous static RAM, 2.2 V to 3.6 V
summary: A 1 Mbit CMOS static RAM organised as 128K bytes, with a plain asynchronous parallel bus: 17 address lines, 8 data lines, two chip enables of opposite sense, an output enable and a write enable. Access is 45 ns over 2.2 V to 3.6 V and -40 °C to +85 °C. Active current is 1.3 mA typical at 1 MHz; deselected it draws 1 µA typical, and it keeps its data down to 1.5 V at 3 µA max. It comes in a 450-mil SOIC, a TSOP I and an STSOP, all 32 pins.
key_figures: 1.3 mA typ, 2.0 mA max at 1 MHz; 11 mA typ, 16 mA max at fmax
VCC down to 1.5 V, 3 µA max

operation.text: An asynchronous CMOS static RAM of 131,072 bytes. Seventeen address lines, A0 to A16, pick a byte; eight lines, I/O0 to I/O7, carry it in both directions. There is no clock: a read or write follows the control pins directly, with 45 ns access.

Two chip enables, CE1 active LOW and CE2 active HIGH, must both be asserted for the device to respond. Either one released deselects it: the I/O lines go to high impedance and supply current falls to the standby figure, more than 99 % below active. CE1, CE2 and OE together provide for memory expansion.

With the chip selected, WE HIGH and OE LOW, the byte at the address on A0 to A16 is driven onto I/O0 to I/O7. In an address-controlled read (chip held selected, OE LOW) new data is valid tAA after the address changes and the old data holds for tOHA. In an OE- or CE-controlled read the data is valid tACE after CE asserts and tDOE after OE falls; the outputs leave high impedance after tLZOE / tLZCE and return to it within tHZOE / tHZCE.

With the chip selected, taking WE LOW stores the byte on I/O0 to I/O7 at the addressed location. The write lasts while CE and WE are both active; either can start or end it, giving WE-controlled and CE-controlled write cycles. Address must be stable tSA before the write starts and tHA after it ends; data needs tSD setup and tHD hold against the ending edge. The I/O drivers are off during a write. If OE is HIGH they stay off; if OE is LOW they turn off tHZWE after WE falls and come back tLZWE after it rises, and no data may be driven onto the I/O lines while they are still outputs. A chip enable released at the same moment WE goes HIGH leaves the outputs in high impedance.

Supply current drops when the addresses stop toggling, and drops to standby (1 µA typical, 4 µA max at 3.6 V) when the chip is deselected. Supply current moves between ICC and ISB at the 50 % point tPU after CE asserts and tPD after it releases. The standby limits need CE1 and CE2 at CMOS levels (within 0.2 V of a rail); the other inputs may float.

VCC may be lowered to 1.5 V with the chip deselected and the data is kept, drawing at most 3 µA. The chip must be deselected tCDR (0 ns min) before VCC leaves VCC(min), and held deselected until tR (45 ns min) after VCC is back at VCC(min). Coming out of retention, VCC should rise linearly from VDR to VCC(min) over at least 100 µs, or rest at VCC(min) for 100 µs, before full-speed operation.
Full AC operation assumes the supply ramps from 0 to VCC(min) in 100 µs and then has 200 µs to settle.
